title: History of Political Thought
description: A study of one or more important figues from the history of political thought.

title: Moral Psychology
description: An examination of the nature of desires, emotions, the imagination, and other aspects of human psychology, and of the ways these bear on the moral evaluation of people and actions.

title: Contemporary Philosophy
description: A study at the graduate level of selected topics in contemporary philosophy.

title: Advanced Topics in Feminist Philosophy
description: A study at the graduate level on topics in feminist philosophy, sometimes covering one topic or one author over the course. Content will vary but may include contemporary debates, such as gender, pornography, consent, single authors such as Wollstonecraft, or de Beauvoir, themes, such as early feminist thinkers, or feminist epistemology

title: Aesthetic Theory
description: A study at the graduate level of the development and analysis of the basic concepts employed in criticism of the arts.

title: Normative Ethics
description: An examination of what makes actions morally right or wrong and people morally good or bad.

title: Meta-ethics
description: An examination of problems concerning the meaning and justification of moral judgments.

title: History of Ethics
description: A study of one or more historically important moral philosophers.

title: Topics in the Philosophy of Religion
description: A study at the graduate level of topic in the philosophy of religion.

title: Philosophy of Law
description: An introduction to some of the main issues generated by the philosophical question, What is law? 1. In what sense is conduct made obligatory by theexistence of law? 2. What, if any, is the relationship between law and morals? 3. What are rules? What does it mean to say that a rule exists? Do courts really apply rules or merely pretend to do so?

title: Advanced Topics in the Philosophy of Law
description: Advanced topics in the philosophy of law.

title: Punishment and Responsibility
description: An examination of some of the philosophical problems of punishment and responsibility: the rationale of punishment and the legal doctrine of mens rea; the analysis of conditions of responsibility, relations between punishment, responsibility, retribution, guilt, shame, etc.

title: Philosophy of Economics
description: An introduction at the graduate level to conceptual and methodological issues surrounding modern economics. Topics may include the scientific status of economics, the use of economic models, the connection between economics and moral theory, and notions of preference, choice, well-being, and rationality in economics.

title: Action Theory
description: An examination of philosophical topics connected with human action, e.g. the role of intentions and desires in the explanation and justification of action and the nature of practical reasons.

title: Topics in Ethical Theory
description: A study at the graduate level of topics in ethical theory.

title: Topics in Theory of Knowledge
description: A study at the graduate level of topics in th theory of knowledge.

title: Topics in Philosophy of Language
description: A study at the graduate level of topics in the philosophy of language.

title: Topics in Philosophy of Mind
description: A study at the graduate level of topics in the philosophy of mind.

title: Topics in Metaphysics
description: A study at the graduate level of topics in metaphysics.

title: Pre-Socratics
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of the pre-Socratic era.

title: Plato
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Plato.

title: Aristotle
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Aristotle.

title: Socrates
description: A study at the graduate level of Socrates and his place in Greek philosophy. The course focuses mainly on Plato's Socratic dialogues but may also treat Socrates' predecessors (principally the Sophists) and contemporary views of Socrates in other authors.

title: Hellenistic Philosophy
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of the Hellenistic philosophers.

title: Descartes
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Descartes.

title: Spinoza
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Spinoza.

title: Leibniz
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Leibniz.

title: Locke
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Locke.

title: Berkeley
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Berkeley.

title: Hume
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Hume.

title: Kant
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Kant.

title: Kant
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Kant.

title: Hobbes
description: This course examines the philosophy of Thomas Hobbes (1588-1679).

title: Nietzsche
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Nietzsche.

title: Wittgenstein
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Wittgenstein.

title: Heidegger
description: A study at the graduate level of selected writings of Heidegger.

title: Frege
description: An examination of the work of the german philosopher and logician, Gottlob Frege.

title: Early Analytic Philosophy
description: A study of one or more major philosophers from the early stages of the analytic tradition (e.g. Frege, Moore, Russell, Wittgenstein, and the logical positivists.)

title: American Philosophy A
description: An examination of the roots and early development of American philosophy with special attention paid to the theory of natural rights, its role in the founding of the nation, and the movement to abolish slavery.

title: American Philosophy B
description: An examination of the development of American philosophy in the 19th and early 20th century, with special attention paid to Pragmatism (e.g. the philosophical writings of Peirce, James and Dewey) and modifications of the theory of natural rights in response to the Darwinian revolution in biology.

title: Other Philosophers
description: Course content will vary. Philosophers not taught in a regular course or seminar, whose work is considered important, will be studied at the graduate level.

title: Historical Philosophers
description: Examination of historical philosophers beyond those covered in Philosophy 106 and 151-166.

title: Philosophical Psychology
description: A study at the graduate level of selected problems in philosophical psychology.
